questions.prompt: Which best describes a computer network?

options.text: Two or more devices connected so they can exchange data
A website you open in a browser

questions.explanation: A network is two or more hosts connected by links so they can exchange data. A website is an application that runs over a network, not the network itself.

questions.prompt: Why is data split into packets rather than sent as one continuous stream?

options.text: So many hosts can share links, packets can be routed independently, and only lost pieces are resent
Because computers cannot store large files
To make the data encrypted automatically
Because routers can only understand text

questions.explanation: Packetization lets many conversations share the same links, allows packets to take different routes, and means a single lost packet can be resent instead of the whole file.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are examples of hosts on a network? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A host is any device connected to the network — laptop, printer, phone. A protocol is a set of rules, not a device.

questions.prompt: The agreed-upon set of rules for the format and order of network messages is called a ____.
questions.explanation: A protocol is the set of rules two hosts follow so they can understand each other's messages.

questions.prompt: Match each networking piece to what it does.

pairs.right: A device connected to the network
The cable or radio connection between devices
Connects hosts within one local network
Connects different networks to each other

questions.explanation: Hosts connect via links; switches join hosts inside a network; routers join separate networks.

questions.prompt: Order the steps a packet takes when your laptop sends a message across the internet.

items.text: The message is split into addressed packets
A packet reaches your home router
Routers relay it hop by hop across networks
The destination's router delivers it to the target host
The target reassembles the packets into the message

questions.explanation: Data is packetized, sent to your router, relayed hop by hop by routers, delivered by the destination network, and reassembled at the target host.
